page-title.purpose: H1 in PageHeader. One per screen. Bold, tracking-tight. The 24px small variant is for sub-pages.

section-heading.purpose: H2 with an amber Heroicons icon. Splits a page into named regions.

body.purpose: Default text size. Anything a user reads at a glance is 16px. Cap at 65–75ch where prose-like.

label.purpose: Form labels, button text, primary metadata. The 14px tier as a deliberate choice — not a default.

meta.purpose: Captions, timestamps, helper text, 'last synced X ago'. The quietest tier; lives in ink-faint.

shadows.name: ring-hairline-light
shadows.purpose: Default card edge in light mode. Almost invisible until you look.

shadows.name: ring-hairline-dark
shadows.purpose: Default card edge in dark mode.

shadows.name: card-default
shadows.purpose: Light-mode card lift. Just enough to separate from the page surface.

shadows.name: card-dark
shadows.purpose: Dark-mode card. Inset highlight simulates a top facet under ambient light.

shadows.name: button-rest
shadows.purpose: Hairline lift on every button variant. Makes the chip feel pressable.

shadows.name: nav-active-inset
shadows.purpose: Active nav item presses in rather than out. Dark mode uses 0.35 opacity.

shadows.name: modal-lift
shadows.purpose: The only place the system genuinely lifts. Modals are loud about being modal.

shadows.name: menu-popover
shadows.purpose: HeadlessUI Menu and Disclosure popovers — workspace switcher, profile dropdown.

shadows.name: hover-ring-action
shadows.purpose: Interactive card hover. The 2px Attention Red ring IS the hover affordance — no scale, no shadow change.

motion.name: ease-quart-out
motion.purpose: Canonical ease-out curve. Used on the modal entrance, banner slides, and pending pill.

motion.name: duration-menu-enter
motion.purpose: HeadlessUI Menu and Disclosure popover entrances.

motion.name: duration-menu-leave
motion.purpose: HeadlessUI Menu and Disclosure popover exits — leave faster than enter.

motion.name: reduced-motion-floor
motion.purpose: Global override applied via `prefers-reduced-motion` media query. All transitions and animations collapse to this.

narrative.overview:
Tayaway is the friend who hands the group exactly what they need, exactly when they need it. The interface is not a place to hang out; it is a place to settle a question, file an expense, or check whose turn it is — then leave. Every screen is a hand-off. Most of the surface stays calm and quiet so the actionable thing reads loudly: a soft white field, a hairline ring, muted body text, and then a single warm-and-bright punctuation — the red button, the amber nav, the cyan link — that tells you what to do next.

The system is Restrained as a color strategy with a deliberate bright-action exception: 90%+ of any screen is hushed neutrals, and the remaining slice is intentionally vivid. Layout is flat at rest with thin rings and small ambient shadows; depth shows up only when something is acting (a hover, a modal, a pending pill). Typography is Inter Variable used at body size by default — small text is a deliberate choice, not a default. Light and dark mode are equal citizens, both designed for the same hand-off feel.

This system explicitly rejects engagement-driven social aesthetics, enterprise/configuration-heavy chrome, and the hero-metric / identical-card-grid clichés.
keyCharacteristics: Flat at rest, lifts only on interaction
Light and dark mode equally first-class

rules.name: The Bright-Action Rule
rules.body: Only buttons, focus rings, the nav bar, and pending-state indicators carry full saturation. Everything else stays in neutrals. If two saturated elements appear in the same viewport, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Two-Hue Restraint
rules.body: A single screen uses CRT Amber or Attention Red at full strength, not both — the nav already carries amber, so the page-level action layer leans on red. Cyan is permitted alongside either, because it reads as a link rather than an action.

rules.name: The No-Decoration Rule
rules.body: Color never decorates. If a color is on screen, it carries meaning — orientation (amber), attention (red), link (cyan), or state (red/green/amber tint).

rules.name: The Body-Size-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Primary content uses 16px. text-sm and text-xs are intentional choices for secondary metadata, never reflexive defaults.

rules.name: The Single-Family Rule
rules.body: Inter Variable for everything. No display face, no monospace — Inter has tabular figures when alignment matters.

rules.name: The Calm-Field Rule
rules.body: Static content is flat and ringed; saturated lift is reserved for things you can act on. If a card is glowing without being clickable, the glow is wrong.

rules.name: The Press-Don't-Lift Rule
rules.body: Active states press in (inset shadow, brightness-95), they don't pop out. The exception is hover — hover gets a ring, never a translation.

rules.name: The Quiet-Surface Rule
rules.body: Cards, inputs, modals, and section bodies stay in neutrals. Saturation belongs to actions and states. A card themed with a brand color is a violation unless it is the action or urgent variant.

rules.name: The One-Action Rule
rules.body: Each card or modal carries at most one Primary button. Secondary actions are TextButtons or the secondary button variant. If you need two primaries, you are showing two screens.

dos: Do keep ≥90% of any screen in neutrals. The bright voices (CRT Amber #d97706, Attention Red #e11d48, Navigator Cyan #0891b2) earn their saturation by being rare.
Do put focus-visible:outline-rose-500 on every interactive element. The Attention Red ring is the system-wide focus signal.
Do use Inter Variable at 16px for primary content. Reach for text-sm / text-xs only for secondary metadata.
Do lead each screen region with a SectionHeading — text-lg semibold plus a text-amber-600 icon.
Do design dark mode at the same time as light mode. Both are first-class.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion. The modal already collapses 200ms to 0.01ms; new motion must do the same.
Do show what matters now. Surface the active event phase (voting, chores, expenses) as the dominant UI.
Do announce state with icon + text + color, not color alone.
donts: Don't add likes, hearts, comments, activity feeds, post-style entries, follower counts, or any other engagement-loop pattern.
Don't ship configuration-heavy chrome — no 'configure your view', no view-builder, no settings the user shouldn't have to think about.
Don't use the SaaS template aesthetic: no gradient hero, no sidebar shell, no identical card grids, no hero-metric template.
Don't use side-stripe borders (a colored border-left as a stripe). This is the system's strongest absolute ban.
Don't use gradient text. Solid color, weight, and scale carry hierarchy.
Don't use glassmorphism or backdrop-blur as decoration.
Don't layer cards inside cards. Nested cards are always a structural mistake.
Don't reach for a modal first. Inline expansion, progressive disclosure, and dedicated routes beat modals for most state.
Don't put two saturated colors at full strength in the same viewport.
Don't size primary content at text-sm. If it matters, it's 16px.
Don't decorate. If a color, icon, or shadow is on screen, it carries meaning.
Don't add fine print, 'learn more' links to nowhere, marketing-tone microcopy, or hedge language.
Don't use bouncy or elastic motion. Ease-out only — cubic-bezier(0.25, 1, 0.5, 1) is the canonical curve.
Don't animate CSS layout properties. Transform and opacity only.
